A cada persona se le permite hablar por tres (3) minutos. Hay un intérprete para su conveniencia.

Staff recommends City Council 1) award a Construction Management Contract to Civil Source, Inc. in the amount not to exceed $67,120 and authorize the Mayor to execute the Agreement as shown in Attachment 5 of the staff report. This option means the expenditures related to Construction Management (CM) services will be reimbursed; and 2) select a firm that submitted a proposal for CM services for this project as shown in Attachment 6 of the staff report. The City Council would need to set the level of compensation for such CM services if different from what is proposed. Expenditures made for CM services under this option would not be federally reimbursable as shown in Attachment 7 and the City Council would need to authorize the use of other City funds such as Gas Tax, Prop 1B, or Prop C, or a combination thereof (need not be the General Fund) for this CM contract; and 3) appoint a City Council committee to perform a review of CM Proposals and recommend an award of a CM contract for City Council consideration at a future date, or re-initiate the RFP process. minutes_text:
CITY COUNCIL
MINUTES
CITY OF BALDWIN PARK
CITY COUNCIL
WEDNESDAY, JUNE 02, 2010
7:00 p.m. COUNCIL CHAMBERS
14403 E. Pacific Avenue
Baldwin Park
Manuel Lozano, Mayor/Chair
Ricardo Pacheco, Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Marlen Garcia, Monica Garcia, Susan Rubio Council Members/Members
Maria Contreras, City Treasurer Alejandra Avila, City Clerk
The CITY COUNCIL of the City of Baldwin Park met in REGULAR SESSION at the above time and place.
CALL TO ORDER
INVOCATION
Led by Pastor Jackson
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ANNOUNCEMENTS
Mayor Lozano adjourned in memory of Jesus Jimenez Sr., father of Jesus Jimenez Jr., a Baldwin Park Police Explorer. Mayor Lozano asked that something be done to assist the family during their time of need. He also adjourned in memory of the father of Recreation & Community Services Commissioner Martha Reyes
Councilmember Rubio expressed her condolences for Corina Dominguez, Baldwin Park resident who had taken her life. Mayor Lozano gave details on her services, which were taking place out of state.
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco adjourned on behalf of former Councilmember David Olivas’ brother
PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS
Ken Woods , resident & business owner addressed comments previously made by Mayor Lozano; he took issue that the Council did not mention Memorial Day and spoke about the significance of the service of those in the military
Cecelia Bernal , resident disagreed with speaker Woods and expressed her pride in the Council for recognizing the military. She invited the Council to closing ceremonies for East Side Little League
Luis Cruz , principal of Baldwin Park High School thanked the Council for acknowledging student athletes at a prior meeting and expressed his pride in working with a School Board and Superintendent who supported the school, and the Council for supporting the students and their achievements
Cecelia Lee , business owner read a statement from Arizona Governor Jan Brewer related to recent acts of violence with those crossing the borders illegally
Greg Tuttle , business owner spoke about immigration issues, comments made by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco and SB 1070
Teri Muse , representing Waste Management shared a sample of the "Bagster" for disposing of bulky items. Mayor Lozano asked that information on the Bagster be be put in the NOW
John Rios , resident thanked CEO Singhal for the improvements at two empty lots in the city and noted that he was seeing improvements at Walnut Creek Nature Park
Public Communications were closed at 7:16 p.m.
Mayor Lozano spoke about the military service of his family members and did not appreciate the Council being questioned on their patriotism. He announced the erection of a monument in recognition of Atanacio Haro-Marin, Rudy Salas and Gabriel Figueroa, fallen Baldwin Park servicemen
Mayor Lozano spoke about comments and gestures made by individuals who were not residents of the city and expressed his intent to report these actions to the Jewish foundation.
He expressed his pride in being a Baldwin Park resident and spoke about civil rights and a multicultural armed forces. He believed that it was a disgrace to insult the City Council and that they would continue to move the city forward. He also stated that immigration reform is needed. He expressed his disappointment that actions and comments are made in the presence of children at the meetings.
Mayor Lozano stated that certain individuals’ businesses should be boycotted for the mean spirited things that they say and do at Council meetings
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco spoke about family who fought and died in service to their country and did not want to be told that he or the Council did not appreciate the military. He spoke about the Hometown Heroes military banner program which recognized Baldwin Park residents who were serving our country.
He expressed his regret that the funds were not available to have a larger event on Memorial Day, mentioning that the City hosted a very large event on Veterans Day, and further stated that the City Council supported the military and did not want anyone to think that they did not.
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco stated that illegal immigration is an emotional issue and expressed his belief that the borders needed to be secured. He believed that we should have a legal system that everyone obeys and individuals want to come here for a better life. He hoped that those who had malicious reasons for coming here were detained. He stated his disagreement to SB 1070 and spoke about old laws that were discriminatory to certain groups of people.
Mayor Lozano spoke about Arizona Governor Jan Brewer and that several police departments in the state of Arizona were not in agreement with SB 1070 and may not enforce it
Councilmember Rubio expressed her agreement that it was a heated and emotional issue. People were losing sight of the fact that we are human beings, and should move forward with respect and don’t bring any more hatred to the issue
Councilmember Marlen Garcia said that this was an opportunity to educate the youth on the injustices that have taken place in the past and that if we didn’t put a stop to it, these practices would continue. She said that she always told her children that they should continue to be proud Mexican-Americans
ROLL CALL
Present: Councilmember Marlen Garcia, Councilmember Rubio, Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco, Mayor Lozano.
Absent: Councilmember Monica Garcia.
Also Present: Chief Executive Officer Singhal, City Attorney Pannone, Recreation & Community Services Director Carrillo, Community Development Manager Castagnola, Public Works Director Galvez, Chief Hadsell, Finance Director Quijano, City Clerk Avila, City Treasurer Contreras, Deputy City Clerk Nieto.
A motion was made by Mayor Lozano and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco to excuse Councilmember Monica Garcia from the meeting
PROCLAMATIONS, COMMENDATIONS & PRESENTATIONS
* Recognition of Baldwin Park Senior of the Year Rosie Rodriguez and BPACE Senior of the Year Willa Reynolds
Mayor Lozano, joined by the Council, Clerk and Treasurer presented plaques to the seniors of the year
* Recognition of the Jean Marie Carpenter Scholarship recipients
Diana Beltran, Kaiser Permanente shared background on the scholarship and its recipients. The Mayor, joined by the Council, Clerk and Treasurer presented certificates to the honorees
* Recognition of the 2010 St. John the Baptist King David Carrillo and Queen Jessica Guerrero
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco shared background on the King and Queen and, joined by the Mayor, Council, Clerk and Treasurer, presented certificates to King Carrillo and Queen Guerrero
* Recognition of the 2010 Baldwin Park Relay for Life Committee members
Mayor Lozano, joined by the Council, Clerk and Treasurer acknowledged the efforts of the committee and presented them with certificates. Mayor Lozano announced that a picture of the committee would be placed in the NOW and requested that a special recognition be given to Annette, the 2-year old who participated in the relay
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion: Approve CONSENT CALENDAR
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco.
1. WARRANTS AND DEMANDS
Staff Report
City Council received and filed.
2. PROPOSED RECOGNITIONS BY THE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL FOR THE PERIOD OF JUNE 2, 2010 - JUNE 15, 2010
Staff Report
City Council approved the preparation and presentation of the plaques, proclamations and certificates as outlined in the staff report.
3. MINUTES
Staff Report
City Council approved the minutes of the special meeting of May 19, 2010.
4. CLAIM REJECTIONS
Staff Report
City Council rejected the claims of Cirilo Rodriguez and the Subrogation demand for National General Insurance Company and directed staff to send the appropriate notice of rejection to claimant.
5. 2nd READING - ORDINANCE NO. 1329
Staff Report
City Council waived further reading, read by title only and adopted on second reading Ordinance No. 1329 entitled, "AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 91 OF THE BALDWIN PARK MUNICIPAL CODE, RELATING TO POLICE RESPONSE TO FALSE ALARMS AND RECOVERING COSTS RELATED TO RESPONSES TO FALSE ALARMS."
REPORTS OF OFFICERS
6. FISCAL YEAR 2010/2011 CITY, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION AND HOUSING AUTHORITY BUDGETS (See related Item #3 on the Community Development Commission Agenda and Item #1 on the Housing Authority Agenda)
Staff Report
Proposed Budget
Director Quijano presented the report to the Council, which was a balanced budget with a small surplus
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco wanted to clarify that the funds for transportation and capital improvements came from other sources and that was what was covered the $4 million budget for capital improvements. He inquired if the reserve would be higher than what they were shown in the study session.
Director Quijano explained that the information was being presented differently, now showing a beginning and ending balance.
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco wanted to make sure that the mid-year budget tied in the goals and objectives set by each department to rate successes. He expressed the desire to see some type of report, possibly on a quarterly basis. He had reservations about the budget regarding take-aways from the State and what type of impact it would have on the city, but supported the budget as presented.
Motion: Approve Fiscal Year 2010-11 budget as presented and waive further reading, read by title only and adopt Resolution No. 2010-019 entitled, "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK ADOPTING THE BUDGET OF THE CITY FOR THE FISCAL YEAR COMMENCING JULY 1, 2010 AND ENDING JUNE 30, 2011".
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco.
ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER
* Request by Councilmember Rubio for discussion on the following
Request for Council discussion and direction to staff to dedicate a page / section of the Baldwin Park NOW to highlight the athletic and academic achievements of students in the community
Council member Rubio said that she was extremely proud of the academic and athletic accomplishments of the students in the area and asked that the Principals assist in providing information to the City
7. AWARD A CONTRACT FOR CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT OF THE RAMONA "A" ROADWAY REHABILITATION - I 605 TO FRANCISQUITO, FEDERAL PROJECT NO. ESPL-5323 (018) - FTIP NO.: LAES411 (Continued from May 19, 2010)
Staff Report
Motion: Appoint Councilmember Monica Garcia and Councilmember Rubio as the City Council committee to perform a review of CM proposals and recommend an award of a CM contract for City Council consideration at a future date, or re-initiate the RFP process.
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco.
8. AWARD A CONTRACT FOR CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT OF THE RAMONA "B" ROADWAY REHABILITATION - FRANCISQUITO TO MERCED, FEDERAL PROJECT NO. ESPL-5323 (019) - FTIP NO.: LAES415 (Continued from May 19, 2010)
Staff Report
Motion: Appoint Councilmember Monica Garcia and Councilmember Rubio as the City Council committee to perform a review of CM proposals and recommend an award of a CM contract for City Council consideration at a future date, or re-initiate the RFP process.
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco.
CITY COUNCIL / CITY CLERK / CITY TREASURER / STAFF REQUESTS & COMMUNICATIONS
* Request by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco for discussion on the following:
Request for City Attorney to provide a legal opinion on project labor agreements
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco spoke about project labor agreements and the benefits they provide. He asked that the City Attorney provide the Council with guidelines as to how project labor agreements could be of use in the City.
Councilmember Rubio expressed her support of Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco's request
City Treasurer Contreras requested that she and City Clerk Avila’s names be included in the NOW as they too were proud of the city that they represented
ADJOURNMENT
There being no other matters for discussion the meeting was adjourned in memory of Jesus Jimenez Sr. and Corina Dominguez at 8:15 p.m.
Approved as presented by the Council at their meeting held July 21, 2010.
Laura M. Nieto, CMC
Deputy City Clerk
